html:
Hvalsey Church, in the old Eastern Settlement of Greenland, is the best preserved Norse ruin in the country. In September 1408 it hosted a wedding between two Icelanders, the last event recorded in writing from Norse Greenland.

The stone church was built in the early 1300s on a large farm. Its walls and gables still stand among the grass.

Letters about the wedding survive because the couple later settled in Iceland and needed proof of their marriage. After that, ships stopped coming and the settlement faded from view. When Hans Egede arrived in 1721 to find the Norse, only ruins and Inuit remained. Hvalsey is part of the Kujataa UNESCO World Heritage Site.
